name: Urnes Stave Church
description: Perched above Lustrafjorden in western Norway, Urnes is a wooden stave church from the 12th century, with some timbers dating back to the late 1000s. Its north doorway is the star: swirling, slender animals twist through carved planks in a style named after the church itself. Inside, rounded arches and cylindrical columns echo the stone churches of medieval Europe, while the carvings blend Viking-era imagery with Christian faith.
